correctness.rationale: For uniformly bounded nonnegative modulations, the Jacobi symmetrization is an analytic bounded-operator family near zero with an isolated simple largest eigenvalue 1/2. Contour projection gives rank-one eigenvectors, graph path restrictions force coordinate vanishing \(q^{j(j-1)/2}\), recurrence gives leading products, and a uniform summable tail validates Hellmann–Feynman integration. This yields the explicit \((d_k^2-c_k^2)/4\) times the common prior squared product at order \(q^{k(k+1)}\) for every k; \(k=1\) and zero later coefficients are covered. Finite-section decimal checks test, but cannot prove, the infinite assertion. A reconstruction formula follows by comparison with finite truncation.

value.rationale: A scalar analytic observable, the numerical radius of a geometrically damped infinite-dimensional shift, reconstructs every member of an arbitrary bounded positive coefficient sequence. Sharp triangular emergence at orders 2,6,12,20,... explains detectability of deep weights despite interference from all later edges; it directly addresses identifiability behind recent multi-parameter geometric shift computations. High-order ill-conditioning is acknowledged and no broad inverse stability claim is made.
